# Pandora's Box: Economic Retaliation in the Russia-Ukraine Conflict

## Russian President Vladimir Putin has accused Kyiv of opening 'Pandora's box' with its strikes on Russian economic targets, warning of retaliatory strikes on Ukraine's economic sectors. This escalates a campaign that began with Ukrainian drone strikes targeting Russian infrastructure, further straining the fragile geopolitical landscape in Eastern Europe.

[Devdiscourse News Desk](/devdiscourse-stories)

In a stern warning, Russian President Vladimir Putin accused Ukraine of provoking a new wave of economic hostilities. He stated that Kyiv's recent strikes on Russian economic targets have opened 'Pandora's box', prompting promises of retaliation against what he termed as Ukraine's most sensitive economic sectors.

The conflict has intensified as Ukraine escalates its campaign of drone attacks on Russian infrastructure, focusing on oil refineries and online retail warehouses. The moves are aimed at crippling the parts of Russia’s economy that Ukraine claims are fueling the Kremlin’s military ambitions.

Putin assured that despite challenges in grain exports, Russia would prevent global food shortages, sidestepping issues caused by the termination of a Turkish-brokered Black Sea grain deal. Meanwhile, he reiterated Russia's openness to peace talks, emphasizing discussions based on 'realities on the ground'.

(With inputs from agencies.)

## Iran-US tensions are intensifying as Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian calls for an end to the month-long war while insisting that Tehran is negotiating from a position of strength. US President Donald Trump, however, says Iran is interested in a deal but is not yet ready to make what he considers the “right deal.” Trump has also claimed that the United States has total control of the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world’s most strategically important waterways. The comments come as Washington increases economic and maritime pressure on Tehran. Iran has rejected the latest US pressure campaign and warned that further threats could trigger a strong military response. Iranian officials say Tehran remains prepared to defend its strategic waterways and interests across the region. Meanwhile, the United States is expected to announce new sanctions targeting Iran, while discussions involving Iran and Oman continue over possible conditions for resuming talks, including security and freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.

# Trump wants more economic pressure on Iran. What are his options?

WASHINGTON — U.S. President Donald Trump has vowed to hit Iran hard economically, after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that Washington would impose measures on Tehran that have "never been seen" as soon as next week.

Bessent is due to hold a press conference at ​2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT) on Monday.

The United States, ‌United Nations and European Union have applied sanctions, implemented trade embargoes and frozen assets since the late 1970s over Iran's nuclear program, human rights violations and support for militant groups.

Since the Iran war began in February, Washington has levied additional maritime, energy and financial sanctions and started a naval blockade.

Data from the U.S. Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) shows the agency has imposed sanctions on more than 1,000 people, vessels and aircraft since Trump began his second term.

Recent measures have targeted Iran's shadow oil fleet; shipping insurers; entities and people enabling Iran's acquisition of weapons; and digital exchanges, freezing an estimated $500 billion in Iran-linked cryptocurrency.

![U.S. Navy sailors work on the flight deck of the aircraft carrier USS George Washington as it transits the Arabian Sea to support U.S. military operations in the war with Iran August 20, 2026.]()

Iran has denounced U.S. plans to announce new sanctions that ​could put further strain on the Islamic Republic's economy.
